title: Specified integral coefficient presentation encoding
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with its valuation ring and uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $X$ a scheme with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $B=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], as in [sk-def-pe-derived-completion], and $\widehat B=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$, using the coefficient construction of [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] without its auxiliary finite-field convention. Reconstruct the section-ring sheaf $B_{\rm sec}$ and the section-action equivalence $S:\operatorname{Mod}_{\rm int}(B)\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(B_{\rm sec})$ by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. An integral presentation encoding consists of a specified ring-sheaf isomorphism $\alpha:B_{\rm sec}\simeq\widehat B$, an equivalence $F:\operatorname{Mod}_{\rm int}(B)\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(\widehat B)$ whose forward functor is exactly $S$ followed by scalar restriction along $\alpha^{-1}$, and additivity of its forward and inverse functors. Its derived equivalence is the termwise localization of this equivalence, using [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This is a bundle of supplied data, with no assertion or choice of an encoding; finite-projection normalization is imposed by the comparison theorem.
